newsitem.title: UK: London freight - BFI posts first gain for two week.
newsitem.headline: London freight - BFI posts first gain for two week.

text.p: The first rise in the Baltic Freight Index (BFI) for a fortnight, up 5 to 1,419, has signalled a halt to the decline on the majority of panamax trades, brokers said.

Except for the earliest positions in the U.S. Gulf, panamax grain rates have become fairly steady in the Atlantic, although the impact of the strikes/lockouts in Santos/Paranagua has so far been hard to assess.
Early positions for capers have been described as weak in the Atlantic, although stronger for April, while the Pacific was steady for both March and April.
The Baltic Handy Index fell one point to 1,076.
Brokers however believe that prospects for geared tonnage were fairly positive, especially in the Far East.
GRAIN - Both Frapaco and Lorentzen were said to have covered stems of 54,000 heavy grain U.S. Gulf/Japan for first half April at $24.25, up 25 cents.
There were also reports that unnamed charterers had since bid $24.35 for this position. Paper has been traded at $24.90 for March and $26.00 for May, both combo.
Frapaco was said to be quoting early April U.S. Gulf/Japan position, but reports that Joyous World 69,286 dwt had fixed U.S. Gulf/Japan at under $24.00 no combo could not be verified.
Toepfer fixed the 1989-built Caribbean Sky for 50,000/10 grains 53' Paranagua/Continent for mid-March at $16.50. The last done in this trade being Angelic Grace (built 1971) at $16.75.
Cargill booked two panamaxes on this route on private terms.
Maritime Wisdom 73,657 dwt was believed fixed Brazil/S.Korea on subjects on timecharter.

In the east, Amorgos 65,105 dwt was said to be fixed by the Australian Wheat Board delivery prompt Kunsan trip via Australia and Mina Qaboos redelivery Muscat at close to $10,500 daily, while the Hanjin-relet Deerpool 65,163 dwt was thought taken by Seabon delivery prompt Inchon for a trip via Australia.
The Seabon was to carry grain to Iran at $10,900 daily.

In the handy section, Tradigrain privately fixed one vessel on timecharter and one voyage basis with grain from N.France to Iraq (Umm Qasr), and Medmar was reported to have taken a vessel of 1.2million cuft bale for bagged cargo from the Continent to Port Sudan at $10,750 daily.
Toepfer fixed Iguana 35,267 dwt from the Plate to the Continent, and Chios Charm 26,541 dwt was fixed Plate/Caribbean, both on private terms.
New business included Dreyfus 50/100,000 grains U.S. Gulf/ARA for end March.
Other new business was, NSAC 54,000 heavy grain Plate and Brazil/Japan or S.Korea Apr/May, Cargill 22,500/25,000 wheat U.S. Gulf/Algeria March 22/27.
MINERALS - Some firmer rates were reported for capers, with Leopold LD at $9.25 for 150,000 ironore Port Hedland/Constanza for April 15/30.
Hoogovens was said to have paid a premium for 140,000 tonnes from Ponta do Ubu and Tubarao to Ijmuiden for end March but full details were not forthcoming.
British Steel's fixed Clymene 65,000 dwt delivery prompt Inchon trip via Australia to UK, thought to be at $7,000 daily).
K Line was said to have taken panamax tonnage for coal and period business in the east, and Halla booked Bechet 65,418 dwt prompt China for a Nopac round on subjects.
In the Atlantic, Stalo 73,000 dwt open W.Italy was covered privately for Atlantic business.

Possibly the weakest fixture of the day, illustrating the soft early position in the U.S. Gulf, was CSK Unity to Cho Yang for 59,000/10 coal to Taiwan for March 17/25 at $19.30, the vessel was said to be waiting up to 10 days for this business.
HANDY-SIZES - Brokers continued to report brighter prospects for modern handies in the Far East.

However, fixtures have been slow to emerge. On the continent Compass Rose was said to have taken Crio 19,643 dwt delivery Hamburg March 10/17 trip Atlantic Colombia at close to $5,250 daily, and Athina P 22,274 dwt was booked on private terms for fertilizers from the Continent to Brazil.
BIFFEX futures traded 253 lots by the end of the day. The most active month April sold 87 lots and traded last at 1,570.
-- Stephen Grainger +44 171 542 8074.
